speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what rehabilitation measures are young sex offenders subject to in their time in prison or probation to prevent recidivism; (b) whether studies are being done on the mindset of local sex offenders, be they for crimes with or without physical contact with victims, to improve the necessary corrective actions; and (c) whether there are plans to work with universities and schools to conduct outreach and introduce relevant material into the curriculum.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Sex offenders in prison also attend other programmes, such as those to build better relations with their families, which will help their overall rehabilitation and reintegration.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The family and community play a key role in providing support for and monitoring the progress of the probationer.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Examples of interventions include the Positive Adolescent Sexuality Treatment Programme and the Positive Psychotherapy Group.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They equip the probationers with skills to improve their relationships, emotional coping and sexual regulation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SPS and MSF will continue to strengthen their programmes based on research and evidence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There are also ongoing efforts by the Singapore Police Force (SPF) to engage schools and universities to prevent sexual offences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SPF will continue to work with schools and universities to raise awareness of sexual crimes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: There is public perception that university students tend to get away with their crime easily.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For example, a 31-year-old man caught taking an upskirt video of a woman at Woodlands Checkpoint was jailed four weeks in December 2019, whereas a 25-year-old National University of Singapore (NUS) student was suspended for photographing two female students in the shower – no jail term.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Regardless of income levels or backgrounds, we take every crime seriously.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: So, it is not wise to draw conclusions based on one or two cases.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: It is important that we send a very strong message that the rich do not get away easily or lightly for any type of crimes, including sexual offences.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: It is, if you are in a university, you got bright future, we do not want ruin your future, so you get away easily.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: As a society, we need to look at this issue frankly, but my answer still stands.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We should not draw certain conclusions based on one or two cases.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: But it is an important issue that we need to address together – whether you are rich or you are educated, you do not get away easily.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The law applies regardless of our background or income levels.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: And it is important that we continue to dispel such misperceptions.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: And if there are specific instances or cases that the Member would like answers, perhaps the Member could file a separate Parliamentary Question (PQ) and we could give it the proper treatment.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned that during the probation, we do get the family involved in the rehabilitation process.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Do we get the family involved in the rehabilitation process while they are in prison as well?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, the question is whether we have family functional therapy for inmates currently incarcerated for sex offences.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: But in most, it involves the offender having to address his or her own criminogenic needs or risks.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: The short answer to the Member's question is yes, there are family programmes, but not all interventions would involve the family.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: There are different modules, and different individuals require different types of treatment.
